newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 17.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The written commitment from the European Commission yesterday that accession talks with Cyprus would begin six months after the end of the inter-governmental conference - in April 1998 - comes as a rebuff to threats from the new Turkish deputy premier. "Cyprus cannot be held hostage to Turkish policy," Commissioner Hans van den Broek said.

--The national economy and development ministries have entered the fray with conflicting statements on the operation of the market, following charges from the foodstuffs industry that supermarkets were taking advantage of the industry.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis was critical of past PASOK governments for fostering a climate in the agricultural sector that relied solely on state support.

--The government is to ask industry and retailers to not increase their prices above 2-2.5 percent next year as part of efforts to contain inflation and get Greece into economic and monetary union. The plan, dubbed "a national responsibility initiative", was discussed at yesterday's high-level meeting on budgets.
--Pharmacists open their doors for the first time in a week today but say they may close them again if the government fails to meet their demands.
--If ruling party PASOK deputies continue to mutiny in Parliament, they may find themselves facing the party's disciplinary council, according to reports.

--Taxpayers will be facing an additional 790 billion drachmas in taxes next year as well as restricted wage increases. The 1998 budget was the focus of discussions at yesterday's meeting, although no binding decisions were made. Other issues discussed included the indexation of tax brackets.

--New cost-cutting measures to be discussed at 'social dialogue' between government, unions and employers include lesser state contributions to child-care centres, holiday camps, spa therapies and funerals.
--Two Greek astronauts have returned from Russia where they received training at the Yuri Gagarin Centre.
--Cabinet has approved the appointment of 25,604 new limited contract civil servants. Most will be employed by the education ministry.
--An investigation is continuing into allegations of mismanagement of Church property and funds. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
